findings.title: Lightweight-token check uses the session-context client instead of the client session's client
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the access token is lightweight by calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). The token being created is associated with the client session available from clientSessionContext, and that client may be different or the session-context client may be unset in some flows. This can cause a NullPointerException or encode the wrong token type. The client used for the token should be taken from the client session / token creation context.

findings.title: Access token ID matcher checks the grant shortcut with the wrong index and inverted logic
findings.body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId is intended to verify that the encoded access token ID contains the expected grant shortcut. The encoded format is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut(2) + ':' + rawId, so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6). The code checks substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals the expected shortcut. As written, the matcher does not validate the grant shortcut correctly and can pass even when the encoded grant is wrong, weakening the event tests for code-to-token, refresh, device, and CIBA flows.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and does not validate rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted despite the constructor contract. Later encoding concatenates the null value and can produce a token ID ending in ':null', breaking the assumption that the raw token ID is a generated unique identifier.

findings.title: New non-default getShortcut method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI interface, but getShortcut is added as a new abstract method without a default implementation. Existing third-party implementations compiled against the previous interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut. This is an SPI/API compatibility break.

findings.title: Public OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor removed
findings.body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context. Extensions or custom grant implementations that used this constructor will fail to compile against the new version or fail at runtime with NoSuchMethodError. If the removal is intentional, it is an SPI/API break that should be called out or replaced with an explicit alternative.

findings.title: Unsafe cast of all OAuth2GrantType provider factories to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates over all provider factories for OAuth2GrantType and casts each one to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. If an extension provides a ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType> that does not implement OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, server startup will fail with ClassCastException. The code should filter for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances or otherwise validate the factory type.

findings.title: Null or malformed grant shortcuts are not validated before being stored
findings.body: postInit puts the value returned by OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut directly into ConcurrentHashMaps. If a factory returns null, the server fails with NullPointerException instead of a clear startup error. There is also no validation that shortcuts are non-null, two characters long, and safe for the token ID encoding. Invalid shortcuts will cause encoding/decoding failures later rather than a clear configuration error.

findings.title: setFormParams does not update the cached grantType
findings.body: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is initialized from formParams in the constructor, but setFormParams replaces the form parameters without recalculating grantType. If setFormParams is used after construction, getGrantType returns the grant type from the old parameter map, and that stale value can be written into ClientSessionContext and encoded into the access token ID.

findings.title: Shortcut Javadoc says 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut says the shortcut is usually like a 3-letter shortcut. The token ID encoder, however, reserves exactly two characters for the grant shortcut and rejects encoded contexts that are not six characters total. Implementers following the Javadoc could provide a three-character shortcut and break token ID encoding/decoding.
